title: The Efficacy of Orally Administrated Probiotic Formula in Preventing a Recurrence of a Urinary Tract Infection During Pregnancy
brief_summary: Background: Urinary tract infections (UTIs), the most common infection in pregnancy,are associated with several maternal and fetal complications, including maternal septic shock, preterm labor, intrauterine growth restriction and intrauterine fetal death. Thus, the prevention of UTIs in pregnancy is a very important goal. Several studies have suggested that alterations in the vaginal flora were associated with recurrent UTIs, and probiotic administrations may have a role in preventing those infections. Nevertheless, this has never been tested in pregnant women.
raw_criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Above 18 years old
* Pregnant women who suffered from at least one episode of UTI
* Women less than 34th week of gestation at the time of the enrollment
* Urine culture is sterile in the beginning of the study

Exclusion Criteria:

* Immunocompromised women
